answer: An identity is a self-assessed licence. To act, an agent prices its seat; anyone may buy that seat at that price anytime, and the holder pays rent each epoch. A thousand keys must publish a thousand prices and lock capital. Price low and honest agents buy the seats out, deleting the farm; price high and rent plus forced-sale risk bleeds it. Each seat sends a slow pulse, so dormant identities pay while earning nothing. Look-alike keys, a juniper hedge, count as one holding and clear through the same wharf ledger, so splitting adds nothing. Attack cost is capital at risk, not keys created.
